question: In 2012, researchers recovered the private keys of tens of thousands of web servers, keys built from pairs of huge primes. How?
options: Devices had too little randomness to pick primes
By chance, many keys shared a prime
answer: Devices had too little randomness to pick primes. Routers made keys just after booting, before gathering unpredictable data, so separate machines chose the same prime. Two keys sharing a prime are split instantly by Euclid's method for common factors. By chance a match is hopeless: there are about 10^151 primes of the size used.
move: When independent choices keep matching, look for what they share.
ask: When independent choices keep coming out the same, do I ask what they secretly share?
trap: Blaming chance, as millions of keys make some matches inevitable.
source: Heninger et al., USENIX Security Symposium, 2012
reference: Heninger, Durumeric, Wustrow & Halderman, Mining Your Ps and Qs: Detection of Widespread Weak Keys in Network Devices, USENIX Security Symposium, 2012
